sections.heading: History
sections.wikitext: After a decline in popularity from the height of their success in the mid-1970s, the Captain and Tennille signed with [[Casablanca Records]] under the guidance of [[Neil Bogart]]. "Do That to Me One More Time" was a comeback for the duo, but they failed to achieve further success on Casablanca and their contract was not renewed. Vocalist and songwriter [[Toni Tennille]] played the song for Bogart at her house with husband [[Daryl Dragon]] in [[Pacific Palisades, California|Pacific Palisades]], [[California]] on an electric piano. Bogart reacted enthusiastically, saying: "That's a smash! There's no doubt in my mind that's going to be your first single."<ref name="Bronson">[[Fred Bronson|Bronson, Fred]] (2003). ''The Billboard Book of #1 Hits'', 5th Edition (Billboard Publications), page 521.</ref> According to ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'', the song is about sex, specifically "male virility."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/list/959432/the-50-sexiest-songs-of-all-time|title=The 50 Sexiest Songs Of All Time|author=M. Tye Comer|author2=Mariel Concepcion|author3=Monica Herrera|author4=Jessica Letkemann|author5=Evie Nagy|author6=David J. Prince|name-list-style=amp |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=February 11, 2010 |access-date=October 13, 2016}}</ref> According to Toni Tennille, she wrote the song about how she felt for Daryl Dragon; however as she put it, "the funny thing was, later on he told me that he never paid any attention to the lyrics... so he didn't know what I was saying".<ref>Studio 10. (2016) ''Toni Tennille on Studio 10.'' YouTube. [online] Available at: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jw0kA7h4VZE (Accessed: December 24th 2023).</ref>
sections.text: After a decline in popularity from the height of their success in the mid-1970s, the Captain and Tennille signed with Casablanca Records under the guidance of Neil Bogart. "Do That to Me One More Time" was a comeback for the duo, but they failed to achieve further success on Casablanca and their contract was not renewed. Vocalist and songwriter Toni Tennille played the song for Bogart at her house with husband Daryl Dragon in Pacific Palisades, California on an electric piano. Bogart reacted enthusiastically, saying: "That's a smash! There's no doubt in my mind that's going to be your first single." According to Billboard, the song is about sex, specifically "male virility." According to Toni Tennille, she wrote the song about how she felt for Daryl Dragon; however as she put it, "the funny thing was, later on he told me that he never paid any attention to the lyrics... so he didn't know what I was saying".

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: The song is performed in the key of [[C major]]. The key changes to [[D major]] for the final chorus and ending. It moves at a [[tempo]] of 90 beats per minute in [[Time signature|common time]]. The vocals span from E<sub>4</sub> to B<sub>5</sub>.<ref>{{cite web |last=Tennille |first=Toni |title=Captain & Tennille "Do That To Me One More Time" Sheet Music |url=https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0068714 |access-date=September 5, 2022 |website=Musicnotes|date=October 20, 2008 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Key & BPM for Do That To Me One More Time by Captain & Tennille |url=https://tunebat.com/Info/Do-That-To-Me-One-More-Time-Captain-Tennille/0m4jVVZrsv0bLkAr1uM6UG |website=Tunebat}}</ref>

sections.heading: Release and reception
sections.wikitext:
"Do That to Me One More Time" became Captain & Tennille's second and final number-one hit (also their final Top 40 song in the U.S.) when it reached the pinnacle of the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart the week ending February 16, 1980.<ref name="Bronson"/> The song had logged four consecutive weeks in the runner-up position on this chart behind [[Michael Jackson]]'s hit "[[Rock with You]]" before ascending to the top of the chart. The song spent a single week in the pole position before being succeeded on February 23 by [[Queen (band)|Queen's]] "[[Crazy Little Thing Called Love]]". Overall, "Do That to Me One More Time" spent 27 weeks on the Hot 100.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/captain-tennille/chart-history/hsi/ |title=Captain & Tennille - Chart History {{!}} Billboard |publisher=Billboard |date= |access-date=9 February 2018}}</ref> 

The song also achieved some crossover success on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks|adult contemporary]] and [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|R&B charts]]. It was their highest-charting hit on the [[UK Singles Chart]], where it reached number seven in March 1980. It also peaked at number three in Australia and was number one in the Netherlands.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dutch Charts - dutchcharts.nl |url=https://dutchcharts.nl/weekchart.asp?year=1980&date=19800308&cat=s |access-date=September 5, 2022 |website=dutchcharts.nl}}</ref>

''[[Record World]]'' called "Do That to Me One More Time" a "warm & tender pop-[[adult contemporary|a/c]] gem."<ref>{{cite magazine|magazine=Record World|date=October 27, 1979|access-date=February 11, 2023 |title=Hits of the Week|page=1|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/70s/79/RW-1979-10-27.pdf}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Stereogum]]'', Tom Breihan criticized the song due to perceiving the lyrics about married sex to be too sleazy and described the production as "ugly and antiseptic late-'70s easy-listening nothingness", scoring the song 2/10.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |date=2020-03-16 |title=The Number Ones: The Captain & Tennille’s “Do That To Me One More Time” |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2076627/the-number-ones-the-captain-tennilles-do-that-to-me-one-more-time/columns/the-number-ones/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=Stereogum |language=en}}</ref>
sections.text:
"Do That to Me One More Time" became Captain & Tennille's second and final number-one hit (also their final Top 40 song in the U.S.) when it reached the pinnacle of the Billboard Hot 100 chart the week ending February 16, 1980. The song had logged four consecutive weeks in the runner-up position on this chart behind Michael Jackson's hit "Rock with You" before ascending to the top of the chart. The song spent a single week in the pole position before being succeeded on February 23 by Queen's "Crazy Little Thing Called Love". Overall, "Do That to Me One More Time" spent 27 weeks on the Hot 100. 

The song also achieved some crossover success on the Billboard adult contemporary and R&B charts. It was their highest-charting hit on the UK Singles Chart, where it reached number seven in March 1980. It also peaked at number three in Australia and was number one in the Netherlands.

Record World called "Do That to Me One More Time" a "warm & tender pop-a/c gem." Writing for Stereogum, Tom Breihan criticized the song due to perceiving the lyrics about married sex to be too sleazy and described the production as "ugly and antiseptic late-'70s easy-listening nothingness", scoring the song 2/10.

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext:
The record was reviewed in the 19 February 1988 issue of ''Black Radio Exclusive'' by Duff Marlowe. Marlowe called the song an exciting version and was getting hot action all across black radio. There were rave reviews by program directors across the US.<ref>''Blak Radio Exclusive'', Volume XIII, No. 5 February 19, 1988 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/BRE/80s/BRE-1988-02-19.pdf Page 30 MUSIC REVIEWS ''By Duff Marlowe'', RENA—DO THAT TO ME ONE MORE TIME—SEDONA]</ref>

According to Deborah Sims, the program director for [[WBLK]] in Buffalo, New York, Rena Scott's "Do That to Me One More Time" was the perfect adult record.<ref>''Billboard'', February 27, 1988 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/80s/1988/BB-1988-02-27.pdf Page 10 ''Radio'', THE OUTA' BOX, BLACK/URBAN]</ref>

sections.text:
As per the 11 December 1987 issue of Black Radio Exclusive, Scott's single was added to the playlist of WIKS in New Bern, NC, WPAL in Charleston, SC, WGOK in Mobile, AL, WZAZ in Jacksonville, FL, and WKXI in Jackson MS.
It was reported by Billboard in the magazine's 12 December issue, Hot Black Singles Action, Radio Most Added section, that "Do That to Me One More Time" by Rena Scott had a total of fourteen add-ons.

sections.wikitext: As per the January 18 - 31, 1988 issue of ''The R&B Report'', Rena Scott's single had been added to the playlists of R&B stations, WDAS in Philadelphia, WLUM in Elm Grove, WGPR in Detroit,<ref>''The R&B Report'', Jan. 18 - 31, 1988 Vol. 1, No. 23 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/R&B-Report/1988/R&B-Report-1988-01-18.pdf Page 43 ''THE R&B PLAYIISTS'', ''<small>Hots and Adds</small>'', WDAS/Philadelphia 215/878-2000, A RENA SCOTT; WLUM/Elm Grove 414-786-1590, A RENA SCOTT; WGPR/Detroit 313/259-8862, A RENA SCOTT]</ref> and WEDR in Miami.<ref>''The R&B Report'', Jan. 18 - 31, 1988 Vol. 1, No. 23 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/R&B-Report/1988/R&B-Report-1988-01-18.pdf Page 44 ''THE R&B PLAYIISTS'', ''<small>Hots and Adds</small>'', WEDR/Miami 305/633-1487, A RENA SCOTT]</ref> The song's radio action was recorded in the 2 February issue of ''[[Radio & Records]]'' in the Urban Contemporary New & Active section. The song was having one heavy rotation, eighteen medium rotations and seventeen light rotations.<ref>''Radio & Records'', Issue Number 723 February 5, 1988 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Archive-RandR/1980s/1988/RR-1988-02-05.pdf Page 62 R&R NATIONAL AIRPLAY, URBAN CONTEMPORARY, NEW & ACTIVE, RENA SCOTT "Do It To Me One More Time" (Sedona/JCI) 36/3]</ref>  It was also no. 2 on the New Artists chart with 36/3 in Reports/Adds.<ref>''Radio & Records'', Issue Number 723 February 5, 1988 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Archive-RandR/1980s/1988/RR-1988-02-05.pdf Page 62 R&R NATIONAL AIRPLAY, URBAN CONTEMPORARY, NEW ARTISTS, 2 RENA SCOTT/Do It To Me One More Time (Sedona/JCI), 36/3]</ref>
sections.text: As per the January 18 - 31, 1988 issue of The R&B Report, Rena Scott's single had been added to the playlists of R&B stations, WDAS in Philadelphia, WLUM in Elm Grove, WGPR in Detroit, and WEDR in Miami. The song's radio action was recorded in the 2 February issue of Radio & Records in the Urban Contemporary New & Active section. The song was having one heavy rotation, eighteen medium rotations and seventeen light rotations.  It was also no. 2 on the New Artists chart with 36/3 in Reports/Adds.

sections.text: For the week of 16 January 1988, the single debuted at no. 84 on the Billboard Hot Black Singles chart. At week five, on 13 February, it reached its peak position of no. 55. It was still in the chart for the week of 12 March.
